newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat ends mixed despite corn/soybean tumble.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat ends mixed despite corn/soybean tumble.

text.p: CBOT wheat futures closed narrowly mixed despite overhead pressure form a limit fall in the neighboring soy complex, traders said.
"Wheat is acting tremendous. They're buying wheat and selling corn and beans," said Steve Bruce of E.D. and F. Man International.
USDA early Friday issued its October crop report which was bearish for corn and soybeans but bullish for wheat.
USDA cut its forecast for 1996-97 U.S. wheat ending stocks to 470 million bushels from the previous forecast for 506 million.
The government also trimmed its outlook for world wheat ending stocks to 116.53 million tonnes, from the previous forecast for 117.43 million.
But some traders said the cut in stocks should not have been a big surprise.
"They cut the stocks but we expected that to happen. We got a hint of that happening in the stocks (Sep quarterly) report," Bruce said.
Wheat futures closed 1/2 cent per bushel higher to two cents th December up 1/2 at $4.24-1/2. New crop July was down 3/4 at $3.74-1/4.
Wheat should begin a seasonal climb after the recent sharp drop in the market, they said.
"There wasn't anything bearish for wheat this morning and wheat seasonally should be going up," said Vic Lespinasse of Dean Witter Reynolds.

Short term technical indicators also helped put a base under wheat with the 20-day moving average (MA) at Thursday's close at $4.25 for the December acting as a magnet. The four-day MA for Dec Thursday closed at $4.25-1/2, which also provided some upward pull for the nearby December contract.

At the close Friday, the four-day MA for Dec was at $4.26 and the 18-day also was at $4.26. Dec's nine day relative strength index (RSI) was at 44.101 points. Technicians generally view an RSI of 30 or less as near oversold and 70 or better as nearing overbought status.
Wheat futures volume was estimated at 15,000 contracts, up from 9,778 Thursday, according to the CBOT.
Wheat options trading featured LIT America's purchase of 600 December $4.80 calls at 1/2 cent and Refco Inc bought 400 December $4.80 calls at 1/2 cent, traders said.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 5,000 contracts, up from 1,673 Thursday.
